text: In software development, Git branching is an essential tool for managing code. A branch is like a separate workspace where you can add new features or fix bugs without disrupting the main version of your project, often called the 'main' or 'master' branch. When you start a new task, you create a *feature branch*, work on your changes, and commit them. Once your work is complete, the next step is *merging*, which brings your branch's changes back into the main branch. However, before merging, it is common practice to open a *pull request*. This is a request for your teammates to review your code, discuss any issues, and ensure quality. This process forms the core of a *version control workflow*, keeping the project organized and collaborative.
